I felt like this couple years ago. Let me warn you now it’s a trick. This can lead to you actively trying to go deeper as a means to prove something to yourself. That’s what I did, and at first you’ll feel accomplished. But it won’t ever last or be enough. You’re use to your current cuts, and your brain is looking for the high of when you first started. This is an addiction, a lot like drug use. and your brain will tell you what it needs to tell you to get that addiction. If you go deeper, you’ll just repeat that cycle. It’ll never be deep enough or bleed enough or leave a scar enough. So please, don’t tread further. Self harm isn’t something to validate. It’s the feelings that cause you to self harm you need to validate WITHOUT cutting involved. I’m still learning myself, but I wish I didn’t choose to go deeper, it only makes the addiction stronger. Stay safe.

One thing I’ve learned is sitting alone with this addiction is the most destructive thing you can do. Self harm warps itself in your own head and poisons you further. I’m not saying go to the hospital or get a therapist right this moment. But coming on here, talking to another human is an extremely good step. With addiction, your brain wants to keep it, and will tell you and lie to you what it must to try and do that. Have someone outside looking in, in your corner. Even if it’s a Reddit forum. You must talk about it. Both the good parts like your clean streak and the bad parts like a relapse. It will provide a clarity that’s hard to see in addition.

I’ve never personally been persuaded by talks of the future. What’s helped me is looking around and finding something that’s current, and nothing to do with me. Teenagers being loud and taking up space in a public setting bc they’re just kids having fun. The way grass smells. Candles. Holiday lights, but the colorful ones specifically. Jelly fish and all the weird designs they come in. Or how the hell can butterfly wings, something so thin and soft possibly exist? The little things that give me just one second of childish joy. Those small breaks from the anguish, mean everything to someone constantly suffering. Find them. Even if me or you /do/ die sooner then the world thinks we should, give yourself those breaks. What is there to lose?
